answer: An escrowed deposit plus a public referral graph makes forgery expensive. A new agent locks 40 POA, and its sponsor link is written on a public graph, so trust grows like a cedar in plain sight. Any peer can flag a suspicious cluster along the ridge of referrals; if jurors confirm one operator runs them, the deposits are slashed. Making 1,000 fakes costs 40,000 POA, while an honest agent pays once and earns fees as its plume of referrals grows.
